source_text:
{Gal 3,21} Οὐ τοίνυν ἐνδεχόμενον ἀλλ' οὐδὲ εὔλογον ἐπ' ἀναιρέσει τῶν εὐλογιῶν
δεδόσθαι φάναι τὸν νόμον. {Gal 3,23}Ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν, φησίν, οὐκ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀλλ'
ὕστερον. χάριτι τῆς δικαιώσεως ἡμᾶς ἦν θεῷ δοκοῦν ἀπολαῦσαι, εἰκότως τέως
νόμοις ἡ φύσις ἡμῶν περιετειχίζετο κωλυομένη τε καὶ ἀναχαιτιζομένη πρὸς ἑκάστης
ἁμαρτίας ἐνέργειαν, ἵνα εἰς τὴν διὰ πίστεως ἀναπεταννυμένην δικαίωσιν εὐτρεπεῖς
ἐκ τοῦ φρουρίου τοῦ κατὰ νόμον ἀπολυθείημεν.
thought_title: The law as a protective wall until justification by faith
orientation: Gennadius is explaining why the law was given, arguing that it was not meant to nullify the blessings but to restrain sin until the justification by faith was revealed.
pass_a_gloss: It is not possible, then, nor even reasonable, to say that the law was given for the nullification of the blessings. Since then, he says, it was not from the beginning but later that it seemed good to God for us to enjoy the grace of justification, reasonably for the time being our nature was being walled around by laws, being hindered and held back from every activity of sin, so that we might be released from the fortress according to the law prepared for the justification being opened up through faith.

choices.why: The verb conveys the image of a protective wall being built around something, matching Gennadius's argument that the law served as a protective barrier restraining sin.
The verb means to check or restrain, like pulling back a horse by the reins; 'held back' preserves the sense of active restraint against sin.
The noun refers to a fortified place or garrison; 'fortress' captures the protective and enclosing sense of the law as a defensive structure.
The verb means to spread open or unfold; 'being opened up' conveys the sense of the justification through faith being revealed or made accessible.
The adjective means ready or prepared; 'prepared' fits the context of being made ready for the justification through faith.

bible_refs.note: Οὐ τοίνυν ἐνδεχόμενον ἀλλ' οὐδὲ εὔλογον ἐπ' ἀναιρέσει τῶν εὐλογιῶν δεδόσθαι φάναι τὸν νόμον
Ἐπειδὴ τοίνυν, φησίν, οὐκ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ἀλλ' ὕστερον

pass_b_english: It is not possible, then, nor even reasonable, to say that the law was given to nullify the blessings (Galatians 3:21). Since it was not from the beginning but later that God saw fit for us to enjoy justification by grace, Paul says, our nature was for a time being walled around by laws, hindered and held back from every activity of sin, so that, fit and ready, we might be released from the fortress of the law for the justification being opened up through faith (Galatians 3:23).

problems.quote: prepared for the justification that was being opened up through faith
problems.source_quote: ἵνα εἰς τὴν διὰ πίστεως ἀναπεταννυμένην δικαίωσιν εὐτρεπεῖς ἐκ τοῦ φρουρίου τοῦ κατὰ νόμον ἀπολυθείημεν
problems.why: 'prepared for' misrepresents εὐτρεπεῖς (fit/ready); 'being opened up' obscures that justification opens up.
problems.fix: so that, fit and ready, we might be released from the fortress of the law for the justification being opened up through faith
problems.ruling: εὐτρεπεῖς modifies 'we might be released', not 'justification'; ἀναπεταννυμένην means 'opened up', passive modifying δικαίωσιν.

edits.old: so that we might be released from the fortress of the law prepared for the justification that was being opened up through faith
edits.new: so that, fit and ready, we might be released from the fortress of the law for the justification being opened up through faith

problems.why: Same metaphor: wall vs fortress of law; reader may think two different images.

edits.old: our nature was for a time being walled around by laws, hindered and held back from every activity of sin, so that, fit and ready, we might be released from the fortress of the law
edits.new: our nature was for a time being walled around by laws, hindered and held back from every activity of sin, so that, fit and ready, we might be released from that walled fortress of the law

fixed: The English already uses the same metaphor of walling/fortress; the problem is not real, but I made a small adjustment to reinforce the connection between the wall and the fortress.

last_rejected.why: Source has singular 'law' (νόμοις is dative plural but refers to the law system; 'laws' suggests multiple laws, changing sense.
last_rejected.ruling: νόμοις is dative plural; 'laws' is grammatically correct. Disputing singular vs. plural reference is interpretive preference, not error.

last_rejected.why: ἑκάστης is 'each' or 'every individual,' but 'every activity' loses the singular force; more critically, ἐνέργειαν is 'working' or 'operation,' not 'activity.'
last_rejected.ruling: ἐνέργειαν means 'activity/working'; 'activity' is within range. ἑκάστης 'every' is acceptable for 'each.' No meaning lost.

last_rejected.quote: the justification being opened up through faith
last_rejected.why: ἀναπεταννυμένην means 'spread out' or 'unfurled' (like a tent, opening up access); 'being opened up' is vague. More importantly, the syntax suggests 'justification through faith' as a unit, but 'the justification being opened up' obscures that this justification is what is opened up to us.
last_rejected.fix: the justification through faith being opened up
last_rejected.ruling: ἀναπεταννυμένην 'opened up' captures unfurling sense. Syntax preserved: δικαίωσιν modified by διὰ πίστεως phrase. Vague but not wrong.
